children: China will further develop offshore yuan markets and expand offshore yuan liquidity as it promotes the currency's internationalisation, Lu Lei, a deputy central bank governor, said on Thursday.
Authorities will keep offshore yuan liquidity ample and stable, and make the issuance of sovereign bonds and central bank bills in offshore markets a regular practice, Lu told a media briefing.
"The internationalisation of the renminbi (yuan) is a sustained, steady process and an irreversible event," he said.
Lu said the central bank would improve the environment for foreign entities to hold and use the yuan, while actively promoting the use of the digital yuan in cross-border transactions.

Yuan-denominated assets are becoming increasingly attractive to global investors, Lu said, adding that overseas entities currently held more than 11 trillion yuan ($1.64 trillion) of domestic renminbi financial assets.
Lu said China would keep the yuan basically stable and had no intention of seeking a trade advantage through currency depreciation.
